library(amorem)

# Alien species reaching new regions

`alien_invasions` holds the first records of established alien mammals, birds,
insects and plants in regions of the world from 1880 to 2005 (Juozaitienė et
al. 2023, from the database of Seebens et al.). Each record is a one-shot
relational event: species `s` is first recorded in region `r` in year `stop`,
and the pair cannot fire again. The [species-invasion vignette](species-invasion.html)
builds the method on simulated data; this case study applies it to the
observed records. It asks three questions: do species that have already spread
keep spreading, do regions that have received many aliens keep receiving them,
and does the El Niño/Southern Oscillation (ENSO) change the yearly rate of new
records?

```{r data}
data(alien_invasions)
a <- alien_invasions
c(records = nrow(a), species = length(unique(a$species)), regions = length(unique(a$region)),
  first = min(a$stop), last = max(a$stop))
round(prop.table(table(a$taxonomy)), 3)
```

```{r data-numbers, include = FALSE}
after <- mean(a$stop >= 1950)
top_sp <- sort(table(a$species), decreasing = TRUE)
```

`r pct(after)` of the records fall after 1950. The most widespread species,
*`r names(top_sp)[1]`*, has first records in
`r top_sp[[1]]` regions.

## Which regions share their aliens

Two regions that receive the same species are linked by trade, travel or
climate. The network joins each of the 80 regions with most records to the
three regions whose alien species overlap most with its own (Jaccard index of
the two species sets); groups are found by modularity (Louvain).

```{r net-prep, include = FALSE}
reg_n <- sort(table(a$region), decreasing = TRUE)
top <- names(reg_n)[1:80]
sp <- split(a$species, a$region)[top]
J <- outer(top, top, Vectorize(function(x, y) if (x == y) 0 else
  length(intersect(sp[[x]], sp[[y]])) / length(union(sp[[x]], sp[[y]]))))
dimnames(J) <- list(top, top)
keep <- do.call(rbind, lapply(top, function(x) {
  o <- order(-J[x, ])[1:3]; data.frame(from = x, to = top[o], w = J[x, o]) }))
keep <- keep[!duplicated(t(apply(keep[, 1:2], 1, sort))), ]
lay <- layout_graph(transform(keep, w = 100 * w), ids = top, seed = 2)
gsize <- sort(table(lay$group), decreasing = TRUE)
gname <- vapply(names(gsize), function(g) {
  m <- lay$id[lay$group == g]; paste(head(m[order(-reg_n[m])], 2), collapse = ", ") }, "")
gcol <- setNames(pal[seq_along(gsize)], names(gsize))
grp <- setNames(lay$group, lay$id)
within <- mean(grp[keep$from] == grp[keep$to])
```

```{r net, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7, fig.alt = "Network of regions linked by the alien species they share"}
par(mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2.6, 0.5))
nodes <- data.frame(id = lay$id, x = lay$x, y = lay$y, size = as.numeric(reg_n[lay$id]),
                    col = gcol[as.character(lay$group)], label = lay$id)
same <- grp[keep$from] == grp[keep$to]
draw_network(nodes, data.frame(from = keep$from, to = keep$to, w = keep$w,
                               col = ifelse(same, gcol[as.character(grp[keep$from])], "#B4BBC0")),
             label_cex = 0.42, node_scale = c(0.5, 2.4))
for (g in names(gsize)) {   # name each group beside its cluster
  k <- lay$group == as.character(g)
  text(mean(lay$x[k]), max(lay$y[k]) + 0.045, paste(gname[[g]], "group"), col = gcol[[g]], font = 2, cex = 0.72, xpd = TRUE)
}
title_left("Regions that share alien species cluster by geography",
           sprintf("80 regions with most records; each joined to the 3 whose species overlap most (width: Jaccard index); dot size: records; colours: groups found by modularity; %s of links within a group",
                   pct(within, 0)))
```

The `r length(gsize)` groups are: `r paste(sprintf("%s (%s regions)", gname, gsize), collapse = "; ")`.
`r pct(within)` of the drawn links join two regions of the same group.

## When the records arrive

```{r heat-prep, include = FALSE}
r40 <- top[1:40]
r40 <- r40[order(match(as.character(grp[r40]), names(gsize)), -reg_n[r40])]
dec <- seq(1880, 2000, by = 10)
in40 <- a$region %in% r40
H <- table(factor(a$region[in40], levels = r40), factor(pmin(floor(a$stop[in40] / 10) * 10, 2000), levels = dec))
S <- prop.table(H, 1)                                    # each region's records spread over the decades
sub <- a[a$region %in% top, ]
gl <- gname[as.character(grp[sub$region])]
late <- tapply(sub$stop >= 1980, gl, mean)
birds <- tapply(sub$taxonomy == "Birds", gl, mean)
r_late <- cor(late, birds)
```

```{r heat, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7.5, fig.alt = "Share of each region's first records per decade, 40 regions grouped by network group"}
par(mar = c(4.2, 9, 2.6, 6))
ramp <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("#FFFFFF", "#CFE6E6", pal[1], "#0B4F4F"))(64)
image(seq_along(dec), seq_along(r40), t(S[rev(r40), ]), col = ramp, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
      zlim = c(0, max(S)))
cut <- which(head(grp[rev(r40)], -1) != tail(grp[rev(r40)], -1)) + 0.5
abline(h = cut, col = "white", lwd = 3)
rect(0.35, seq_along(r40) - 0.45, 0.48, seq_along(r40) + 0.45, col = gcol[as.character(grp[rev(r40)])], border = NA, xpd = TRUE)
axis(2, at = seq_along(r40), labels = rev(r40), las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.6, line = -0.2, col.axis = ink)
axis(1, at = seq_along(dec), labels = paste0(dec, "s"), tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.65, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.6)
# the share recorded since 1980, per region, at the right
text(length(dec) + 0.6, seq_along(r40), pct(rowSums(S[rev(r40), c("1980", "1990", "2000")]), 0), cex = 0.5,
     col = ink_soft, adj = 0, xpd = TRUE)
mtext("since 1980", side = 3, at = length(dec) + 0.9, line = 0.1, cex = 0.55, col = ink_soft)
# colour scale
zs <- seq(0, max(S), length.out = 64); xs <- seq(1, 4, length.out = 65)
rect(head(xs, -1), -1.6, tail(xs, -1), -1.1, col = ramp, border = NA, xpd = TRUE)
text(c(1, 4), -1.9, pct(c(0, max(S)), 0), cex = 0.55, col = ink_soft, xpd = TRUE)
text(4.2, -1.35, "share of the region's records in the decade", adj = 0, cex = 0.55, col = ink_soft, xpd = TRUE)
title_left("Regions differ in when their aliens were first recorded",
           "share of each region's first records per decade (darker = larger share); right: share since 1980; rows grouped as in the network")
```

Each row shows how one region's first records spread over the decades. The
share recorded since 1980 is `r paste(sprintf("%s in the group of %s", pct(late[order(-late)], 0), names(late)[order(-late)]), collapse = ", ")`.
Across the `r length(late)` groups it correlates at `r fmt(r_late, 2)` with the
share of birds among the records.

The first records five years at a time, between the 60 species recorded in
most regions and the 60 regions with most records, on a fixed layout; each line
joins a species to the region where it is first recorded in the window:

```{r anim-prep, include = FALSE}
br5 <- c(seq(1880, 2000, by = 5), 2006)
lab5 <- paste0(head(br5, -1), "\u2013", tail(br5, -1) - 1)
n5 <- tabulate(findInterval(a$stop, br5), length(br5) - 1)
tcol <- c(Birds = pal[6], Mammals = pal[5], Insects = pal[2], Plants = pal[3])
sp_tax <- tapply(a$taxonomy, a$species, `[`, 1)
actor_col <- c(setNames(tcol[sp_tax], names(sp_tax)), setNames(rep("#4A5560", length(unique(a$region))), unique(a$region)))
sp_n <- sort(table(a$species), decreasing = TRUE)
in60 <- a$species %in% names(sp_n)[1:60] & a$region %in% names(reg_n)[1:60]
a60 <- a[in60, ]
top_reg <- intersect(c("Australia", "Hawaiian Islands", "Taiwan", "United Kingdom", "Lithuania", "Portugal"), names(reg_n)[1:60])
```

```{r anim, echo = FALSE}
anim_events(a60$species, a60$region, a60$stop, breaks = br5, labels = lab5, node_col = actor_col,
            edge_col = tcol[a60$taxonomy], node_label = setNames(top_reg, top_reg), n_nodes = 120,
            title = "First records of alien species, five years at a time",
            sub = "dark dots: regions; coloured dots and lines: species by group (gold birds, rose mammals, violet insects, green plants)",
            fps = 4, alt = "Animation of first records of alien species in five-year windows from 1880 to 2005")
```

Over all species and regions, the busiest window, `r lab5[which.max(n5)]`, holds
`r fmt(max(n5))` first records, against `r fmt(n5[1])` in `r lab5[1]`; the
animation shows `r fmt(nrow(a60))` of the `r fmt(nrow(a))` records.

## Which kinds of species go where

```{r taxa, fig.height = 4.4, fig.alt = "Share of each taxonomic group among the first records of each region group"}
taxa <- c("Birds", "Mammals", "Insects", "Plants")
fl <- table(factor(sub$taxonomy, taxa), factor(gl, gname))
P <- prop.table(fl, 2)
o <- order(P["Birds", ])                               # most birds at the top
tcol <- c(Birds = pal[6], Mammals = pal[5], Insects = pal[2], Plants = pal[3])
par(mar = c(4.6, 14, 2.6, 1))
bp <- barplot(P[, o], horiz = TRUE, col = tcol, border = "white", axes = FALSE, names.arg = rep("", length(o)),
              space = 0.35, xlim = c(0, 1))
axis(2, at = bp, labels = paste0(gname[o], " group\n", fmt(colSums(fl)[o]), " records"), las = 1, tick = FALSE,
     cex.axis = 0.68, col.axis = ink, line = -0.5)
axis(1, at = seq(0, 1, 0.25), labels = pct(seq(0, 1, 0.25), 0), tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.7, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.6)
mid <- apply(P[, o], 2, function(v) cumsum(v) - v / 2)
for (i in seq_along(o)) for (k in taxa) if (P[k, o[i]] >= 0.08)
  text(mid[k, i], bp[i], pct(P[k, o[i]], 0), cex = 0.62, col = "white", font = 2)
legend("bottom", inset = c(0, -0.25), legend = taxa, fill = tcol, border = NA, horiz = TRUE, bty = "n", cex = 0.7,
       text.col = ink, xpd = TRUE)
bird_groups <- colnames(fl)[fl["Birds", ] > fl["Plants", ]]
n_b <- sum(P["Birds", ] > 0.5); n_p <- sum(P["Plants", ] > 0.5); n_m <- ncol(P) - n_b - n_p
num <- c("No", "One", "Two", "Three", "Four", "Five", "Six")
title_left(paste0(num[n_b + 1], if (n_b == 1) " group receives" else " groups receive", " mostly birds, ",
                  tolower(num[n_p + 1]), " mostly plants", if (n_m) paste0(", ", tolower(num[n_m + 1]), " a mix") else ""),
           "share of each taxonomic group among the first records of each region group; sorted by the share of birds")
```

```{r chord-numbers, include = FALSE}
share <- prop.table(fl, 2)
```

Birds outnumber plants among the records of the groups of
`r paste(bird_groups, collapse = "; ")`, where they make
`r paste(pct(share["Birds", bird_groups], 0), collapse = ", ")` of the
records; plants make `r paste(pct(share["Plants", setdiff(gname, bird_groups)], 0), collapse = ", ")`
of the records in the other groups. The groups of the network therefore follow
partly what kind of species a region receives, as well as where it lies.

## A relational event model, 1970–2005

We model the `r fmt(sum(a$stop >= 1970))` first records from 1970 to 2005.
Species and regions are two node sets (`mode = "two"`), and a pair leaves the
risk set once it has fired (`risk = "remove"`); the pairs recorded before 1970
are excluded from the start (`exclude_pairs`). ENSO takes one value per year
for every pair, so the controls are drawn with time-shifted sampling
(`shift = "exponential"`), which gives each control its own year. Starting in
1970 keeps the page fast: the sampler enumerates the at-risk pairs of every
shifted event.

```{r sample}
ev_all <- data.frame(sender = a$species, receiver = a$region, time = a$stop)
ev <- ev_all[ev_all$time >= 1970, ]
prior <- ev_all[ev_all$time < 1970, ]
cc <- sample_non_events(ev, mode = "two", risk = "remove", seed = 1,
                        shift = "exponential", window = c(1970, 2005),
                        exclude_pairs = prior[, c("sender", "receiver")])
c(mean_shift_years = attr(cc, "shift")$mean, events_without_control = length(attr(cc, "shift")$uninformative))
```

Covariates of each row, evaluated at its own time:

- **species spread**: regions where the species was already recorded
  (`sender_outdegree`), counting the records before 1970 (`prior_log`);
- **region pressure**: species already recorded in the region (`receiver_indegree`);
- **taxonomic group** of the species (plants as reference);
- **ENSO**: the annual mean of the Oceanic Niño Index (`oni`, NOAA), the
  instrumental record, in the row's year.

```{r covariates}
cc <- endogenous_features(cc, stats = c("sender_outdegree", "receiver_indegree"),
                          history_log = ev, prior_log = prior)
cc$log_spread <- log1p(cc$sender_outdegree)
cc$log_region <- log1p(cc$receiver_indegree)
tax <- setNames(a$taxonomy, a$species)[cc$sender]
for (k in c("Birds", "Insects", "Mammals")) cc[[k]] <- as.integer(tax == k)
data(oni)
oni_year <- tapply(oni$anomaly, oni$year, mean)
cc$enso <- as.numeric(oni_year[as.character(floor(cc$time))])
aggregate(cbind(log_spread, log_region, enso) ~ event, cc, mean)
```

```{r fit}
cv <- c("log_spread", "log_region", "Birds", "Insects", "Mammals", "enso", "time")
w <- widen_case_control(cc, covariates = cv)
fit <- rem(~ log_spread + log_region + Birds + Insects + Mammals + nl(enso, k = 5) + nl(time, k = 5),
           data = w, method = "gam")
est <- summary(fit)$p.table[, c("Estimate", "Std. Error")]
round(est, 3)
summary(fit)$s.table
```

```{r forest, fig.height = 3.8, fig.alt = "Estimated effects with 95 percent intervals"}
lab <- c(log_spread = "species already widespread", log_region = "region already invaded",
         Birds = "birds (vs plants)", Insects = "insects (vs plants)", Mammals = "mammals (vs plants)")
e <- est[names(lab), 1]; se <- est[names(lab), 2]; y <- length(lab):1
par(mar = c(3.4, 12, 2.8, 1))
plot(e, y, xlim = range(0, e - 1.96 * se, e + 1.96 * se), ylim = c(0.5, length(lab) + 0.5), type = "n",
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
abline(v = 0, col = rule, lwd = 1.2)
segments(e - 1.96 * se, y, e + 1.96 * se, y, col = pal[1], lwd = 2.2)
points(e, y, pch = 21, bg = "white", col = pal[1], cex = 1.3, lwd = 1.6)
axis(1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
axis(2, at = y, labels = lab, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink, line = -0.6)
mtext("effect on the log-rate, with 95% interval", side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft)
title_left("Spread begets spread, on both sides of the pair",
           "effects on the log-rate of a first record, 1970-2005; other terms held fixed")
```

```{r fit-numbers, include = FALSE}
b <- est[, 1]; s <- est[, 2]
ens <- summary(fit)$s.table[1, ]
fit_lin <- rem(~ log_spread + log_region + Birds + Insects + Mammals + enso + nl(time, k = 5),
               data = w, method = "gam")
lin <- summary(fit_lin)$p.table["enso", ]
d_enso <- smooth_data(fit$fit, 1)
out <- d_enso$fit - 1.96 * d_enso$se > 0 | d_enso$fit + 1.96 * d_enso$se < 0
runs <- rle(out); ends <- cumsum(runs$lengths); starts <- ends - runs$lengths + 1
off <- vapply(which(runs$values), function(k) sprintf("from %s to %s °C (%s)", fmt(d_enso$x[starts[k]], 2),
  fmt(d_enso$x[ends[k]], 2), if (mean(d_enso$fit[starts[k]:ends[k]]) > 0) "above zero" else "below zero"), "")
r_enso <- cor(oni_year[as.character(1950:2005)],
              enso_nino34$nino34[match(1950:2005, enso_nino34$year)], use = "complete.obs")
n_years <- length(unique(floor(cc$time)))
```

Holding the other terms fixed, one unit of `log(1 + regions already reached)`
raises the log-rate of a species' next first record by `r fmt(b[["log_spread"]], 2)`
(s.e. `r fmt(s[["log_spread"]], 2)`), and one unit of
`log(1 + species already recorded)` raises a region's by
`r fmt(b[["log_region"]], 2)` (s.e. `r fmt(s[["log_region"]], 2)`). The
taxonomic coefficients compare a species of each group with a plant species of
the same spread: a control species is drawn from all
`r fmt(length(unique(a$species)))` species, most of them plants, and a bird,
insect or mammal reaches a new region at a higher rate per species.

```{r enso, fig.height = 4.2, fig.alt = "Smooth effect of the annual Oceanic Nino Index on the rate of first records"}
par(mar = c(3.4, 3.8, 2.6, 1))
draw_smooth(d_enso, xlab = "annual mean Oceanic Ni\u00f1o Index (\u00b0C)", rug = oni_year[as.character(1970:2005)])
title_left(if (lin[["Pr(>|z|)"]] > 0.05) "No monotone link between ENSO and the rate of first records" else
             "The rate of first records changes with ENSO",
           "smooth effect of the annual ONI, with 95% band; ticks: the 36 years 1970-2005")
```

The ENSO term rests on `r n_years` distinct yearly values. The smooth uses
`r fmt(ens[["edf"]], 1)` effective degrees of freedom (p = `r fmt(ens[["p-value"]], 2)`)
and has no monotone shape; its band leaves zero
`r if (length(off)) paste(off, collapse = " and ") else "nowhere"`.
Entered linearly, ENSO has a coefficient of `r fmt(lin[["Estimate"]], 3)` (s.e.
`r fmt(lin[["Std. Error"]], 3)`) per °C. With so few independent values, a curve
of this shape is also what a year-to-year fluctuation in recording effort
produces, so the data do not support an ENSO effect on the yearly rate. The
annual ONI correlates at `r fmt(r_enso, 2)` with the tree-ring reconstruction
`enso_nino34` over 1950–2005: the two indices are not interchangeable, and the
instrumental one is the closer measure of the years modelled here. The trend
`nl(time)` absorbs the growth of recording effort over the decades.

## What is not in the model

- Distance, trade, colonial history, climate match and land use: the source
  release carries them for every species–region interval (535,020 rows) and
  can be downloaded to fit the full model of Juozaitienė et al. (2023).
- A record dates the first observation, not the arrival; survey effort differs
  between regions and decades.
- The records before 1970 enter only through the history and the exclusion of
  pairs that had already fired.
